howWeMakeVideos.title: How we make videos (one screen)
howWeMakeVideos.intro: Three ways of working make 97% of everything we post in the 90 days. Everything shows the real product. Nothing is bought, faked or generated to look like Makeborne.

ways.name: 1. Record the screen, add the words
ways.covers: Speedruns, demos, tutorials, before and after, 'made from one sentence'
steps: Type one sentence into Makeborne and record the screen while it builds. Never stop the recording.
Record one change in chat, then publish or export.
Open the matching template, drop the recording in, type the words that appear on screen.
If you sped the build up, the little clock says so ('Sped up ×8').
Record your voice over it, add captions, check it on your phone, post.
ways.time: About 2 hours the first time, 1.5 hours after that

ways.name: 2. Talk to the phone
ways.covers: Day 1, Day 7, Day 30, 'why no free plan', 'who's behind this'
steps: Phone at eye level, window light, say the five lines. Three takes.
Keep the best take, cut the pauses.
Add the 'Day N' tag, the real numbers (typed from Whop, never rounded up) and captions.
Show screen clips in the bottom half only, never over your face.
LinkedIn gets the captioned version without music.

ways.name: 3. Picture posts
ways.covers: Statics, carousels, stories, X cards, link previews
steps: Take a screenshot of a real Makeborne result.
Open the picture template, paste the exact headline from the plan.
One coloured italic word, the price and the refund line at the bottom.
Save one image per page, check it at phone size.
Post, or join the pages into a PDF for LinkedIn.
ways.time: About 25-45 minutes, 1.5-2 hours for a carousel

howWeMakeVideos.everythingElse: The rest is creators (they film themselves, we check the draft), the two brand films, and a small optional test of AI-made opening shots that the owner has to approve first.
rules: Only show what is live today.
Every sped-up build says so on screen.

stack.why: The product is the proof. Real captures in HyperFrames give exact type, honest speed and zero tool cost; the founder's face carries trust; AI video is a small, labelled, optional test for opening shots only.
stack.recommendation: Minimal stack now ($0/month). Decide on a one-month Higgsfield Starter test ($15) at the Sun 8 Nov review.

captureStandards.account: A clean owner account on production makeborne.com used only for marketing: fictional display name, no real e-mail visible, an empty bookmarks bar, a dedicated browser profile, no other tabs. Crop out the account e-mail, avatar, browser tabs and bookmarks. Never show a Whop store page or any unreleased menu item.
captureStandards.desktop: OBS, 60 fps, CQP/CRF high quality. Two window sizes: 1440x900 CSS px at 2x device scale (records 2880x1800) for 16:9 and punch-ins, and 860x1080 CSS px at 2x (records 1720x2160) for vertical-first composer shots. Browser zoom 100%; the 2x comes from the display scale so text is sharp when punched in. Cursor highlight on; system notifications off.
captureStandards.phone: Native screen recording at 60 fps, Do Not Disturb on, battery and time not distracting. For a physical phone in frame: a second phone on a tripod at eye level, window light, no hand blur.
captureStandards.builds: Record every build uncut from Create to finished, and log brief, start and end time (m:ss) and credits in the run log. The uncut file is kept for the 90-150 s full cut, the landing page and the 'uncut build' DM reply. Punch cuts use data-playback-rate and the clock chip states the factor.
captureStandards.names: Every business name a build invents is checked against real trademarks and local businesses before it appears in a public frame (trademark office search plus a web search). Known traps: Tern, Tidal, 'Northface Labs', Galerie Nord, Kazu, Round Nine, Salt & Swell, Petal & Stem.
captureStandards.data: No personal data on screen: blur (12 px Gaussian in HyperFrames, or `npx hyperframes media-treatment`) every real business name, address, phone and e-mail in lead-finder results; crop Whop screens to totals only; handles blurred unless the person agreed.
captureStandards.reencode: Before editing: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -crf 16 -g 60 -pix_fmt yuv420p -an out.mp4` (keyframe every second at 60 fps; seeking never freezes).
captureStandards.storage: Captures go to the private asset library on a local disk, never into this public repository (production/.gitignore blocks media).

pipelines.name: UI speedrun / workflow demo (real screen capture + HyperFrames timer and kinetic overlay)
pipelines.template: T02-speedrun (plus T04 triptych for V10, T01 end card where the script ends on one)
steps: Write the brief on the run sheet (exact text, fictional name), check names, set the capture standard (2x UI, 60 fps).
Record the frame-0 asset first: the finished output as a 390-wide phone scroll (published site) or the finished slide/page.
Record the composer typed by hand in the 860x1080 portrait window, Plan, then Create.
Record the build uncut; log start/end time and credits. Never stop the recording to retry.
Record exactly one chat edit, then Publish and the live Makeborne address in a browser (V02/V04/V57) or Export to PPTX/PDF (decks, books).
`node production/tools/new-project.mjs T02-speedrun <id> --episode <n> --formats 4x5,16x9`, drop captures into assets/capture/, re-encode with -g 60.

Set the variables: hookLine, briefText (verbatim), clockText ('Real time · m:ss' only if data-playback-rate is 1, else 'Sped up ×N' with the same N), three 1-3 word labels, editRequest (verbatim), liveText with the measured total, ctaText per platform.

Record the founder VO to picture (phone voice memo is fine, no music while recording), `npx hyperframes transcribe assets/audio/vo.wav --model small.en`, then `node production/tools/captions-to-html.mjs assets/transcript.json compositions/captions.html --max-words 4 --fix makeborn=Makeborne`.
Music: TikTok CML track (brand TikTok) at 0.14 under voice; IG/YT library track; none on LinkedIn/X. Two or three SFX only on visible actions (click on Create, pop on chip landings).

`npx hyperframes check --json`, `npx hyperframes snapshot --review` (read review-phone.jpg at 360 px), quality bar (section 7), then render 9:16 at 30 fps (`--quality delivery`) and the format variants.
Cut the 60-150 s full build from the same capture (same project, longer build window at 1x or 2x) for TikTok long, LinkedIn 4:5 and the landing page.

pipelines.name: Cinematic hook (Higgsfield shot -> HyperFrames type -> real capture)
pipelines.usedBy: B-variants only, after P-D1: V02-B, V07-B (plate reused by V42-B), V18-B, V40-B, V48-B
pipelines.template: T07-cinematic-hook prepended to the A-variant project
steps: Only for a piece whose A-variant (plain real-UI hook) has been posted and measured, so the test has a baseline.
Write the prompt from this plan (perVideo[].higgsfield): no people, no faces, no hands, no logos, no readable text or signs, no real business, never product UI or outputs.

Generate in Higgsfield Cinema Studio with the named camera preset, 9:16, 5 s, 1080p; at most 3 takes; log model, preset, prompt, credits and date in the rights log; download the paid-plan (unwatermarked) file only.
Trim to the best 2.5 s (data-media-start), keep the AI-generated scene chip on every frame, set the hook type in HTML (never let the model render words).
Hard cut on the beat to the first real capture; everything after the cut is the A-variant unchanged.

Post with the TikTok AI-generated content toggle on (realistic scene), YouTube altered/synthetic = Yes, and expect Meta 'AI info'. Same caption and CTA as A, new utm_content hook code (for example tt-v02-r3b).
Judge at 7 days on /go/ clicks and tracked sales per 1,000 views against the A-variant, never on views alone. Kill the pipeline if 3 of 5 B-variants lose.

pipelines.name: Founder face-to-camera (phone + captions)
pipelines.template: T05-founder (Day-N pill, ledger count-up, b-roll inserts, captions)
steps: Write 4-6 sentences from the script; numbers typed in from Whop and the /go/ report on the day, never estimated or rounded up.
Film 3 takes at eye level with window light (phone on a tripod, 1080p60 or 4K30, lavalier or the phone 30 cm away). First words are the hook.
Pick the best take, cut breaths and dead air; punch-ins (1.00 -> 1.08) on emphasis words; b-roll inserts in the lower half only, never over the face.
Captions are mandatory (LinkedIn plays muted): transcribe, fix names, captions-to-html at 3-5 words per group.
Day-N pill for 3 s; the ledger card only with the real figures; crop or blur every buyer name and e-mail in screen inserts.
LinkedIn 4:5 1080x1350 with captions and no music; TikTok/Reels 9:16; X 16:9 or 1:1 as the post needs.

pipelines.usedBy: All 48 creatives except the four built inside Makeborne; V16 photo-mode stills; video covers
pipelines.template: T09-stills (lay-proof, lay-type, lay-step, lay-end), sizes per creative
steps: Copy the creative's COMPOSE text from data/creatives.json verbatim into the page markup (headline, subcopy, strip). Every letter is HTML; no model redraws UI or type.
Drop the real capture (PNG at 2x) into the capture card; for type-only creatives there is no capture.
One page per 1-second clip; `npx hyperframes snapshot --at 0.5,1.5,... --output stills/<Cid>` writes one PNG per page.
Check at 360 px wide (phone legibility), contrast of #5C616D on canvas for small type, alt text written for each image.

Export at the creative's size; JPEG quality 90 for Meta/IG, PNG for X and LinkedIn.

disclosure.summary: Real screen captures of our own product, the founder filming himself and typeset HTML need no AI label. Labels are required for (1) generated shots that look realistic, (2) concept art shown in films, (3) generated images inside outputs after the images beat, and (4) every paid creator post. A fake customer testimonial by an AI avatar is never allowed.

byPlatform.rule: Turn on the AI-generated content label for any post with a realistic generated scene or person (Community Guidelines effective 24 Sep 2026). Brand account uses the Commercial Music Library only. Paid creators: branded-content toggle plus 'Ad' in video.

Meta adds 'AI info' automatically for content made with its own generative tools or detected through industry signals (C2PA); it appears under 'About this ad'. Use Meta's AI label on organic posts with realistic generated shots. Paid creators: paid-partnership label.

Altered or synthetic content = Yes for photorealistic generated scenes; not needed for captions, upscaling, AI-written scripts, our own real captures or a non-realistic stylised plate. Label shows on the player for photorealistic content.

From 2 Aug 2026: a generated image or video that resembles real people, places or events and could falsely appear authentic is a deepfake: label it clearly at first exposure (the final Code of Practice of 10 Jun 2026 points to an EU icon or equivalent label). Evidently artistic or fictional shots get a lighter disclosure. Makeborne as a provider must also mark its own generated images machine-readably once images ship (gate box 6).

Testimonials must come from real people with real experience; AI-generated reviewers and fake customers are banned (16 CFR 465), and the ASA applies its testimonial rules to deepfakes and synthetic people. Creator posts disclose the material connection in the video itself. Credits for sharing reward the act of sharing, never positive sentiment.

neverAllowed: An AI avatar or synthetic person presented as a customer, user or creator
Our own team posing as unconnected customers
A cloned voice of anyone but the founder (and only with his consent and a description note)
Generated 'screenshots' of Makeborne output presented as real output
A real person or business shown endorsing Makeborne without written consent

realVsAiBroll.finding: No controlled public study compares screen-recorded demos with AI b-roll for SaaS conversion (searched 26 Oct 2026). The evidence that exists points one way: conversion content in this category shows the UI, the finished artifact and a next step (LightReel, Oct 2026); text-plus-product statics lead Meta hit rates (Motion 2026); fully AI-made ads underperform human-made versions of the same briefs on sales impact (Ipsos/Syracuse, May 2026); and AI tells (uncanny visuals, fast montages that hide flaws) trigger backlash (NN/G, Dec 2025).
realVsAiBroll.recommendation: About 90% of posted seconds real: screen captures, the founder, real B-roll. At most 10% generated, only as a 1.5-2.5 s metaphor or context plate before the real UI, never as product proof, always labelled, and always as a measured B-variant against a real-UI A-variant. Judge on /go/ clicks and sales per 1,000 views.
